# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `wtm generate markdown`; do not edit. -->

Worktree manager: a pool of bare git repositories and their worktrees.

Registered repositories are kept as bare repositories in the repos directory. Worktrees are created from them in the checkouts directory.

Standard output only carries data (paths, lists); messages go to standard error.

## Global options

These apply to all commands.

- `--config <FILE>` — Config file [env: WTM_CONFIG] [default: ~/.config/wtm/config.toml]
- `--repos-dir <DIR>` — Directory of the bare repositories [env: WTM_REPOS_DIR]
- `--checkouts-dir <DIR>` — Directory of the worktrees [env: WTM_CHECKOUTS_DIR]

## wtm register

Register an upstream repository

Creates a bare repository named NAME in the repos directory, with SOURCE as its remote, and fetches it. No worktree is created.

SOURCE is a URL, or ACCOUNT:PATH for a repository on an account's service, e.g. `github:owner/repo`. A PATH without owner is the account user's own repository.

```
wtm register [OPTIONS] <SOURCE> [NAME]
```

Arguments:

- `<SOURCE>` — URL of the upstream repository, as given to `git clone`, or ACCOUNT:PATH
- `[<NAME>]` — Name of the repository [default: derived from SOURCE]

Options:

- `--remote <REMOTE>` — Name of the remote (default: `origin`)

## wtm adopt

Turn an existing clone into a registered repository and worktree

Moves the clone's .git directory into the repos directory as the bare repository NAME, and makes the clone's directory a worktree of it. The directory is moved into the checkouts directory, unless --keep-path is given. Branches, stashes, remotes, hooks, uncommitted changes and untracked files are kept.

Refused for clones with linked worktrees or submodules, or with an operation such as a rebase in progress.

```
wtm adopt [OPTIONS] <PATH> [NAME]
```

Arguments:

- `<PATH>` — Top directory of the clone
- `[<NAME>]` — Name of the repository and worktree [default: the directory name]

Options:

- `--keep-path` — Leave the worktree where the clone is

## wtm auth

Manage accounts on upstream services (GitHub, GitLab)

Accounts are kept in the config file. Their tokens are kept by git's credential helpers, the same way git keeps HTTPS passwords.

### wtm auth add

Add an account

Asks for an access token, unless git's credential helper already has one for URL (for example from `gh auth login`). The token is checked against the service and stored with git's credential helper. Without a token, only public repositories can be looked up.

GitHub tokens need the `repo` scope (or read access to the repositories, for fine-grained tokens); GitLab tokens `read_api`.

```
wtm auth add [OPTIONS] <NAME> <KIND>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>` — Name of the account, used as ACCOUNT in `ACCOUNT:PATH`
- `<KIND>` — Kind of service One of: `github`, `gitlab`.

Options:

- `--url <URL>` — Web address of the service [default: https://github.com or https://gitlab.com]
- `--user <USER>` — Your user name [default: the token's user]
- `--protocol <PROTOCOL>` — Clone URL to register repositories with (default: `ssh`)
- `--token-stdin` — Read the token from standard input instead of asking

### wtm auth list

List accounts

```
wtm auth list [OPTIONS]
```

### wtm auth check

Check that accounts' tokens work

```
wtm auth check [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Arguments:

- `[<NAME>]` — Account [default: all]

### wtm auth remove

Remove an account from the config file

The token stays with git's credential helper, since git may use it for HTTPS, unless --forget-token is given.

```
wtm auth remove [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>` — Account

Options:

- `--forget-token` — Also remove the token from git's credential helper

## wtm search

Search repositories on an account's service

Lists repositories you own or are a member of, matching QUERY if given. With --all, searches all repositories visible to you (QUERY is then required). Register one with `wtm register ACCOUNT:PATH`.

```
wtm search [OPTIONS] <ACCOUNT> [QUERY]
```

Arguments:

- `<ACCOUNT>` — Account to search with
- `[<QUERY>]` — Text to look for in names and descriptions

Options:

- `--all` — Search all visible repositories, not just your own

## wtm unregister

Remove a registered repository

Deletes the bare repository. Refused while the repository has worktrees, or has branches with commits that are on no remote.

```
wtm unregister [OPTIONS] <REPO>
```

Arguments:

- `<REPO>` — Registered repository

Options:

- `-f, --force` — Delete even if branches have commits that are on no remote

## wtm repos

List registered repositories and their remotes

The default remote is marked with `*`.

```
wtm repos [OPTIONS]
```

## wtm remote

Manage the remotes of a repository

### wtm remote list

List the remotes of a repository

```
wtm remote list [OPTIONS] <REPO>
```

Arguments:

- `<REPO>` — Registered repository

### wtm remote add

Add a remote and fetch it

```
wtm remote add [OPTIONS] <REPO> <NAME> <URL>
```

Arguments:

- `<REPO>` — Registered repository
- `<NAME>` — Name of the remote
- `<URL>` — URL of the remote, as given to `git clone`

Options:

- `--no-fetch` — Don't fetch the new remote
- `--default` — Make it the default remote

### wtm remote remove

Remove a remote and its remote-tracking branches

```
wtm remote remove [OPTIONS] <REPO> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<REPO>` — Registered repository
- `<NAME>` — Remote

### wtm remote set-default

Set the remote that `new` fetches and tracks by default

```
wtm remote set-default [OPTIONS] <REPO> <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<REPO>` — Registered repository
- `<NAME>` — Remote

## wtm fetch

Fetch registered repositories

Fetches all remotes of the given repositories, or of all registered repositories if none are given. Branches deleted on a remote are removed from the remote-tracking branches.

```
wtm fetch [OPTIONS] [REPOS]...
```

Arguments:

- `[<REPOS>]` — Registered repositories [default: all]

## wtm new

Create a worktree

Creates the worktree NAME in the checkouts directory and prints its path.

The branch checked out is BRANCH if given, else NAME if given, else the default branch of the remote. An existing local branch is checked out as is. Otherwise, if the remote has the branch, a local branch tracking it is created. Otherwise a new branch is created from START (default: the remote's default branch), without upstream.

```
wtm new [OPTIONS] <REPO> [NAME]
```

Arguments:

- `<REPO>` — Registered repository
- `[<NAME>]` — Name of the worktree [default: REPO]

Options:

- `-b, --branch <BRANCH>` — Branch to check out
- `--from <START>` — Start point of a new branch
- `--remote <REMOTE>` — Remote to fetch and track [default: the default remote]
- `--no-fetch` — Don't fetch before creating the worktree

## wtm list

List worktrees

Shows each worktree's repository, branch and state: uncommitted changes, untracked files, commits ahead of or behind the upstream, and commits on no remote.

Alias: `ls`

```
wtm list [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

- `--repo <REPO>` — Only list worktrees of this repository
- `-p, --paths` — Show the path of each worktree
- `--names` — Only print worktree names, one per line

## wtm drop

Remove a worktree and its branch

Removes the worktree directory, including ignored files, and deletes its local branch. Refused if anything else would be lost: uncommitted changes, untracked files that are not ignored, an operation in progress, a lock, or commits that are on no remote.

```
wtm drop [OPTIONS] <NAME>
```

Arguments:

- `<NAME>` — Worktree

Options:

- `-f, --force` — Drop even if something would be lost
- `-k, --keep-branch` — Keep the local branch
- `--fetch` — Fetch first, so recently pushed commits count as pushed

## wtm locate

Print the path of a worktree

Without NAME, prints the checkouts directory. Meant for scripts and shell functions such as `cd "$(wtm locate NAME)"`.

```
wtm locate [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Arguments:

- `[<NAME>]` — Worktree

Options:

- `--repo` — Print the path of the bare repository NAME instead (or of the repos directory, without NAME)

## wtm repair

Re-link worktrees after moving directories

Fixes the links between worktrees in the checkouts directory and their repositories after either directory was moved, and forgets worktrees whose directory was deleted.

```
wtm repair [OPTIONS]
```

## wtm config

Show the effective configuration

```
wtm config [OPTIONS]
```

## wtm shell-init

Print shell integration code

Defines completion for wtm and a function (default `wcd`) that changes directory to a worktree. Add to your shell's rc file, after compinit for zsh:

eval "$(wtm shell-init zsh)"

```
wtm shell-init [OPTIONS] <SHELL>
```

Arguments:

- `<SHELL>` — Shell to integrate with One of: `bash`, `zsh`.

Options:

- `--cd-command <CD_COMMAND>` — Name of the change-directory function (default: `wcd`)
